raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through like I actually do every spring, walking the land and figuring out what I'm going to do.

---

*In my own voice:*

I've been working this same ten mu of land for thirty-five years — my father farmed it before me. Wheat-maize, wheat-maize, every year the same. I don't know about all these new things people talk about. I know what works on my fields because I've seen it with my own eyes.

My son works in the city, comes back for wheat harvest and maize planting when I really need him. Otherwise it's me and the old lady. Ten mu isn't much but it's enough to keep us busy at the busy times. We can't afford to hire people like the big farms do — if we had to pay for all the labor we wouldn't make anything.

**About the wheat** — I planted it back in October, same as always. Right after the maize came off I had them run the big machine through and I put down my base fertilizer. I use compound fertilizer, the kind in the blue bags — one bag per mu at planting, that's what I've always done. Fifty jin of urea per mu at spring topdressing when the wheat "turns green" and starts jointing. I look at the color — if it's yellow I put a little extra, if it's dark green already I hold back. My neighbor Old Zhang, he's been using less the past two years, said it didn't hurt his yield, but I'm not going to risk it. Fertilizer is expensive but a bad wheat crop is worse. Last year I got about four hundred some jin per mu — not bad, not great. The year before was better because the rain came at the right time.

Irrigation — I'll water three times if the sky doesn't help me. Once in early spring before topdressing, once at heading, once at grain filling if it's dry. Each watering costs me money at the well — pumping from that deep well isn't cheap. If it rains I skip one. I can't afford to water just to be safe.

For pests — weeds come up in spring, I spray herbicide once, the "2,4-D" kind everyone uses. Aphids sometimes at heading, I watch for them. If I see them I spray, if not I don't waste the money.

**About the maize** — I plant right after the wheat combine leaves the field. Same week, no time to waste. The earlier the better because maize needs the whole summer. I buy hybrid seed from the agricultural supply store — you have to, can't save maize seed like wheat. Whatever variety they're selling that year, whatever people in the village are planting. Maybe thirty or forty yuan per mu for seed.

Maize doesn't need as much fertilizer as wheat on my land, I've found. I put one bag of compound per mu when I plant, and then maybe thirty jin of urea when the maize is knee-high. If the rain comes enough in July and August I might not irrigate at all. If it's dry I'll water once at tasseling — that's the important time, I learned that from losing half a crop one dry July back in the nineties.

Herbicide after planting, that's standard now. Used to weed by hand when I was young but nobody does that anymore.

**What I'm worried about this year** — fertilizer prices have been going up, I heard. I'll use what I need but I won't buy extra to store. Diesel for the pump is expensive. If the wheat price stays okay I'll be fine. Three of us in the household, my son sends some money, we're not rich but we're not hungry.
